anomalies.observed: The netlist contains two microcontrollers, U1 (ATtiny13V-10S) and U3 (ATtiny45-20P), and every corresponding pin is connected to the same net: U1.6/U3.6 on NET0001, U1.7/U3.7 on NET0003, U1.1/U3.1 on NET0004, U1.2/U3.2 on NET0005, U1.5/U3.5 on NET0007, U1.3/U3.3 on NET0009, U1.8/U3.8 on +5V, and U1.4/U3.4 on GND.
anomalies.expected: The specification describes the board as 'an ATtiny-driven fan controller', implying a single ATtiny MCU. Standard practice is not to parallel two microcontrollers driving the same nets unless one is explicitly an unpopulated alternative footprint; the netlist gives no indication that either MCU is excluded from assembly.
anomalies.impact: If both MCUs are assembled, their outputs can contend on PB0, PB1, PB2, PB4, and PB5, and the shared reset/ISP path may also be driven by two devices. This can cause unpredictable fan-control behavior or damage due to output conflicts.

parsed.summary: The design files appear anomalous because they wire two ATtiny microcontrollers in parallel, while the intended fan controller is described as an ATtiny-driven board with a single MCU.
